chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ala' ibn Razin al-Qalla', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who divorced his wife one time (revocable divorce), then he died while she was in her waiting period. He said: 'She inherits him, then she completes the waiting period of the one who died, which is her husband. And if she died, she inherits him. If he was killed or she was killed while she was in her waiting period, each of the two inherits from the blood-money (diyah) of the other.'
ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance and iddah rules for a wife after a revocable divorce if the husband dies?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal status of a wife in *iddah* following a single revocable divorce (*talaq raj'i*) and her husband's subsequent death, establishing that she inherits him as a full wife. It further elucidates the principle of reciprocal *diyah* (blood-money) inheritance if either spouse dies while the other is in the waiting period, reflecting the continuity of marital bonds until the *iddah* concludes. This ruling is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between the rights of a divorced wife and a widowed wife during the transitional period.
